newsitem.title: USA: Q3 foreign demand for US Treasuries was strong-PSA.
newsitem.headline: Q3 foreign demand for US Treasuries was strong-PSA.

text.p: Foreign demand for U.S. Treasury securities surged in the third quarter of 1996 due mainly to increased buying in Asia, bringing net purchases in the first nine months of 1996 past their level for the full year in 1995, said PSA, the Bond Market Trade Association.

Net purchases in U.S. Treasury securities by foreign official institutions and private foreign investors in 1996 rose to $148.3 billion in the first nine months alone from $134.1 billion in the full year 1995.
Foreign investors now hold 30 percent of the total $3.4 trillion in outstanding marketable US Treasury securities.
Foreign private investors accounted for more than half of the third quarter's purchases, totaling $86.1 billion.

Purchases by foreign official institutions, including central banks, treasuries and ministries of finance, represented $64.5 billion of the total, according to data released by the U.S. Treasury Department.
Purchases in the third quarter surged to $73.5 billion, representing almost 50 percent of total foreign purchases in all three quarters combined.
Asian investors bought $69.4 billion of U.S. Treasuries in the first nine months of 1996, representing 46.8 percent of total Treasury debt sold to non-U.S. investors during that period, the PSA said.

Japanese buying accounted for 37.5 percent of all Asian purchases in the first three quarters of 1996, prompted by regulatory reforms aimed at keeping the yen from rising against the dollar, and relatively higher U.S. interest rates.
Japanese investors bought $26.0 billion in U.S. securities for the first three quarters of the year, compared to $16.9 billion for the full year 1995.
Hong Kong accounted for $5.7 billion in acquisitions of U.S. securities in the third quarter while China accounted for $5.5 billion.

European investors bought $78.4 billion of U.S. Treasury securities in the first nine months of 1996, a 52.9 percent share of total foreign purchases for that period. Europe's net purchases in 1995 totaled $50 billion.

Investors in Latin America and the Carribean were net sellers during the first three quarters of 1996. The sell-off is attributed to the liquidations of long positions in U.S. Treasuries by offshore hedge funds, the PSA said.
-- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679
